title: Gluing compatible affine formal desingularizations
statement: A Noetherian adic formal scheme is a ringed space covered by finitely many $\operatorname{Spf}B$, where $B$ is a Noetherian ring complete and separated for powers of a finitely generated ideal; $\operatorname{Spf}B$ has the primes containing that ideal and the inverse-limit structure sheaf. It is reduced if its chart rings are reduced. Its reduced closed fibre is obtained by quotienting the chart rings by the radical of an ideal of definition. A formal variety in characteristic zero means such a formal scheme whose reduced closed fibre is of finite type over a characteristic-zero field [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; the field structure is not fixed as part of a morphism. In this statement the chart rings are quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring]. A locally principal pair $(\mathfrak X,\mathfrak I)$ has an invertible ideal of definition, locally generated by a non-zero-divisor; it is principal affine if $\mathfrak X=\operatorname{Spf}B$ and $\mathfrak I=(\pi)$ for a single non-zero-divisor $\pi\in B$. Its singular locus is cut out chartwise by the radical ideal of the nonregular locus of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. The pair is rig-regular if this ideal contains a power of $\mathfrak I$. A regular morphism of pairs preserves the distinguished ideal by extension and induces regular ring maps on formal affine charts [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], that is, flat maps with Noetherian geometrically regular residue-field fibres. A formal blowup is the completion of the ordinary blowup of an affine chart along the extended original ideal of definition [def-nagata-global-blowup]. A strong desingularization tower is a finite ordered sequence of these blowups, with coherent nonempty regular centers lying over the singular locus of the original object and regular terminal formal scheme [pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-regular-scheme]. The centers are open if their ideals contain powers of the extended ideal of definition. Compatibility with a regular morphism means that its source tower is obtained from the pullback target tower by deleting exactly the stages with empty centers, retaining every other extended center ideal in its order, even if the associated blowup is an isomorphism. Let $\mathscr C$ have objects finite disjoint unions of reduced rig-regular locally principal formal varieties as above, and morphisms all regular morphisms of pairs, including open immersions. Let $\mathscr P\subset\mathscr C$ be the full subcategory of finite disjoint unions of principal affine pairs, including the empty union. Suppose $G$ is a rule on $\mathscr P$ assigning strong desingularization towers with open centers, compatible with every morphism of $\mathscr P$ as just defined. Then $G$ extends uniquely up to unique isomorphism of ordered towers over the original objects to such a rule on $\mathscr C$. For any finite principal affine open cover $\{U_i\}$ of an object, the extension restricts to the local towers with the stage synchronization specified by the single tower $G(\coprod_i U_i)$; the synchronized towers and their coherent center ideals glue, independently of the cover and its refinements, even when overlaps are not affine. The extension is compatible with every regular morphism of pairs with exactly empty centers removed and all retained ideals in order; its empty value has length zero.

source.place: Temkin arXiv:0904.1592v2, §3.4.1 final paragraph (printed p.25), applying the gluing argument of Lemmas 2.3.1 and 2.3.3 and Remark 2.3.4 (§§2.3.5–2.3.6, printed pp.12–13) to principal affine formal charts, with formal terminology §§2.4 and 3.1.1–3.1.4. Read online 2026-10-24; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Choose a finite principal affine open cover $U_i$ of the input pair. To obtain one, refine a finite formal affine cover on the opens where the invertible ideal of definition has a non-zero-divisor generator; the principal opens supplied by [lem-per-formal-affine-principal-refinement] form a basis, and a finite subcover suffices. By [lem-per-qe-formal-regularity-locality] each subpair is still reduced, quasi-excellent and rig-regular, has a finite-type reduced closed fibre, and its inclusion is regular. Put $A=\coprod_iU_i\in\mathscr P$ and $T=G(A)$, of length $r$. Restrict $T$ to each component WITHOUT contracting it: this retains $r$ ordered positions, with unit ideals where the center is empty. Formal restriction, including restriction of all higher levels, is supplied by [lem-per-formal-open-blowup-base-change].

We need the following synchronization argument, which uses only the assumed compatibility of $G$. For $W,A\in\mathscr P$ and two regular maps $f,g:W\to A$, form $D=W\coprod A$ and the surjective maps $f\coprod1_A,g\coprod1_A:D\to A$. By [lem-per-formal-open-blowup-base-change] every recursive pullback level is a fibre product. Each pulled-back center is nonempty because its component over the identity copy of $A$ is the original nonempty center. Thus neither pullback loses a stage: both are $G(D)$, with exactly the same ordered center ideals. Restrict to the $W$ component. The uncontracted towers $f^*G(A)$ and $g^*G(A)$ coincide, including every empty position. Their comparison is canonical by the rigidity clause of that node. All maps used are regular by [lem-per-qe-formal-regularity-locality].

source.place: Lemma 2.3.1 and Remark 2.3.2; its disjoint-union argument written out

proof.text: Cover each possibly non-affine $U_i\cap U_j$ by principal affine opens $W$ in the intersection, using [lem-per-formal-affine-principal-refinement]; these pairs are in $\mathscr P$ by [lem-per-qe-formal-regularity-locality]. There are two maps $W\to A$, through $U_i$ and $U_j$. Step 2 identifies the restrictions of $T$ over $W$ with their empty positions intact. Inductively suppose the first $k$ levels have been identified on the entire overlap. The two center ideals at position $k$ agree on its cover by the inverse images of the $W$'s, so they agree as ideal subsheaves. The next levels are then canonically identified as the blowup of that same ideal by [lem-per-formal-open-blowup-base-change]. This proves the induction from level zero and gives the overlap comparison on all levels. On triple intersections the composite comparison equals the direct one: both preserve the base and every center, so the rigidity clause forces equality. No affineness of an entire overlap is assumed.

source.place: Lemmas 2.3.1 and 2.3.3; non-affine overlap and cocycle details

proof.text: Construct the global tower by induction on $k\le r$. At $k=0$ it is the given formal scheme. Suppose its level $X_k$ has the inverse-image open cover by the local levels of $T$. Their center ideals agree on intersections by Step 3. Explicitly set $J_k(V)=\{s\in\mathcal O_{X_k}(V):s|_{V\cap U_{i,k}}\in J_{i,k}(V\cap U_{i,k})\ \forall i\}$. This is an ideal sheaf restricting to each $J_{i,k}$; their local finite presentations show it is coherent. It is open: choose local powers of the extended ideal of definition contained in the local center ideals, and take their maximum on the finite cover. Apply [lem-per-formal-open-blowup-base-change] to define $X_{k+1}$ as its global formal blowup. Its restriction is exactly the required next local level, completing the induction. This uses the explicitly stated chartwise meaning of coherent formal ideals; no gluing theorem for ordinary schemes is applied to a formal scheme.

At every position some center of $T$ is nonempty, so the glued center is nonempty; otherwise its restriction to every component of $A$ would be empty. Each local center is either empty or a regular center of $G(U_i)$, because contracting $T|_{U_i}$ gives $G(U_i)$ by the hypothesis on $G$. The glued open center is an ordinary closed subscheme of a finite thick fibre; its local rings are therefore exactly those of these open local center schemes. It is regular. Its image lies in the original singular locus, since the local images do and the singular ideals restrict compatibly by [lem-per-qe-formal-regularity-locality]. The terminal formal level is regular by the same node's locality statement. Empty centers in $T|_{U_i}$ contribute identity arrows; every nonempty center, including one whose blowup is an isomorphism, has been retained. If the input is empty, a nonempty center is impossible, so $G(\varnothing)$ and our constructed value both have length zero.

For cover independence compare $U_i$ and $V_j$ using $D=(\coprod_iU_i)\coprod(\coprod_jV_j)$ and $G(D)$. Step 3 glues this combined synchronized tower. It has no position whose center is empty on all the $U_i$: a nonempty center on a $V_j$ has a point, whose image in the original object lies in some $U_i$; at that point the overlap comparison of Step 3 identifies it with a nonempty center on the $U_i$ side at that very position. Thus restriction to $\coprod_iU_i$ loses no position. The hypothesis on $G$ identifies that entire restriction with $G(\coprod_iU_i)$; the same holds for the $V_j$ side. Step 4 consequently constructs the same ordered tower from either cover. The comparisons are unique by [lem-per-formal-open-blowup-base-change], so they are transitive for three covers. This includes refinements, repeated charts, and the single-chart case, in which the output is $G$ itself.

source.place: Lemma 2.3.3 and Remark 2.3.4; cover and refinement independence

proof.text: Let $h:Y\to X$ be a regular morphism of pairs. Choose a principal affine cover $V_j$ of $X$ and a finite principal affine cover $U_i$ of $Y$ subordinate to the inverse images of these opens, by [lem-per-formal-affine-principal-refinement]. Write $A=\coprod_iU_i$, $B=\coprod_jV_j$. Each restricted map $U_i\to V_{j(i)}$ is regular by [lem-per-qe-formal-regularity-locality]. The map $A\coprod B\to B$ which equals these maps on $A$ and the identity on $B$ is surjective regular. Its recursive pullback of $G(B)$ loses no positions, by the argument of Step 2 and [lem-per-formal-open-blowup-base-change]. Restricting to $A$ shows that $G(A)$ is obtained from the uncontracted pullback to $A$ by deleting precisely those positions whose center is empty everywhere on $A$. Since $A$ covers $Y$, these are exactly the empty global pullback centers. Step 4 glues all other extended ideals in the same order, so this contraction is the tower constructed on $Y$. Cover independence makes the comparison independent of these choices, and the base-change identity/composition clauses make it compatible with compositions.

source.place: §3.4.1 final paragraph; Lemma 2.3.3 functoriality in arbitrary regular morphisms

proof.text: For uniqueness, let $H$ be any extension with the required compatibility. For a principal cover $A=\coprod_iU_i\to X$, $H(A)=G(A)$. Its surjectivity and [lem-per-formal-open-blowup-base-change] imply that pulling back $H(X)$ to $A$ deletes no nonempty center. Thus $H(X)$ has the same stage count as $G(A)$ and the same center ideals on its chart cover. The equalizer description in Step 4 forces its first center to be ours; the canonical blowup comparison then identifies the next level, and induction identifies all levels and centers. Rigidity gives uniqueness of that isomorphism. This proves uniqueness as a rule as well, since the comparisons for each regular morphism are the already established pullback comparisons.

split_report.summary: Kept the given arbitrary compatible principal-affine rule G; proved its extension by the surjective disjoint-union synchronization argument, principal refinements of non-affine overlaps, an explicit induction gluing center ideals and blowups, cover independence, regular functoriality and uniqueness. Added two generic formal-geometric toolkit statements, not replacement resolution functors. No statement change.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q130-82af2662b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes, every cited statement and Temkin arXiv:0904.1592v2 (fetched read-only, since no copy is in literature/): §§2.3.1–2.3.6 with Lemma 2.3.1, Remark 2.3.2, Lemma 2.3.3 and Remark 2.3.4; §§2.4.1–2.4.14 with Lemmas 2.4.4 and 2.4.6, Corollary 2.4.5 and Remark 2.4.2; and §3.4.1, whose last paragraph applies the 'standard gluing argument' that the item states. The statement is unchanged and is Lemma 2.3.3 moved to locally principal rig-regular formal varieties, with Temkin's §2.3.3 rule for removing empty blowups. Step 2 is Lemma 2.3.1: the maps f⊔1 and g⊔1 are surjective, so empty positions sit at the same places. Step 3 covers non-affine overlaps by opens principal in both charts (an exact clause of lem-per-formal-affine-principal-refinement), with an explicit level induction and rigidity for the cocycle. Step 4 glues the center ideals as an equalizer and blows up globally (Temkin 2.4.4). Step 6 is cover independence; I checked that restriction to either cover deletes no position. Step 7 is functoriality through A⊔B→B. Step 8 is uniqueness through the surjective cover. Both new nodes are true, self-contained, statement-only and in the item's unit. lem-per-formal-open-blowup-base-change gives formal blowups, flat adic base change (Stacks 0805 on charts, then completion), rigidity by the universal property, and qe of the blowup by Gabber. lem-per-qe-formal-regularity-locality is Temkin 2.4.3, 2.4.9, 2.4.12 and Lemma 2.4.6, with qe kept as Remark 2.4.2 requires. The chart rings are Q-algebras, because the closed fibre is in characteristic zero and the rings are complete. Neither node is a duplicate or a restated clause. Nearby existing nodes are inputs for their future splits: lem-per-completed-base-regularity (Lemma 2.4.4), lem-per-gabber-adic-quasi-excellence, lem-per-quasi-excellent-formal-affines and def-per-noetherian-adic-formal-system. Statement citations equal stmt_deps, proof_deps equal the union of the uses, and there is no cycle, no SGA and no off-unit statement, so no tool_uses are needed. The WANTED archival copy of Temkin stands.
